title: The Toledo cell (1577)
hook: his own order kidnaps him and locks him in a tiny cell for nine months

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Discalced: Teresa's barefoot friars, and a farmhouse at Duruelo. Today, the reform costs John almost everything.

Ávila, a winter night in December 1577. John is living in a small house beside a convent of nuns, where he serves as their confessor. There's a crash at the door. Men burst in, some of them friars of his own order, some armed. They seize him, take his papers, and lead him away blindfolded to Toledo, to their priory above the river. There they put him in a room and lock the door. He'll be in that room for nine months, and almost nobody knows where he is.
screen: `A WINTER NIGHT IN ÁVILA.` → `SEIZED BY HIS OWN BROTHERS.` → `TAKEN TO TOLEDO.`

segments.voice: First, why. This wasn't a random crime. It came out of a bitter fight inside the Carmelite order. The older branch, often called the Calced, the ones who wore shoes, saw Teresa's reform as a split, and as disobedience to their superiors. The Discalced saw it as a return to the order's first ideals. Church officials gave conflicting orders, and both sides believed they were in the right. John was caught in the middle. It's worth saying: both branches are still part of the Catholic Church today, and they live in peace. Second, the cell. It was a closet, roughly six feet by ten, once used as a storeroom off a guest room. No window, only a narrow slit high in the wall. To read his prayer book, John had to stand on a bench at midday and catch the thin light. In winter it froze. In summer it baked. Third, the treatment. Bread and water, sometimes scraps of sardine. The same habit for months, with lice crawling through it. At first he was brought to the dining hall and beaten while the friars ate, and told that the reform was finished and that Teresa had given up on him. Fourth, what he did. He was ordered to renounce the reform. He refused. And there, in the dark, sick and alone, he began to do something no one expected. That's tomorrow. For now, Jesus's words about the last judgment: "I was in prison, and you came to me."
screen: `A FIGHT INSIDE ONE ORDER.` · `A CLOSET SIX FEET BY TEN.` · `BREAD, WATER, BEATINGS, LICE.` · `ORDERED TO RENOUNCE. HE REFUSED.` · then, large: `I WAS IN PRISON, AND YOU CAME TO ME.`

segments.voice: Hold in mind people locked away right now: in prisons and jails, in detention, held hostage, or shut in by illness, fear or a hard home. You don't have to know their names, but if you know one, hold that one. If you pray, ask God to be with them in their dark room; if you don't, simply remember they're there.
Toledo. The city where John was imprisoned nine months in a closet-sized room of the Carmelite priory, from December 1577. Today's word.
Your line: the dark room. Nine months in the dark, and he never gave in. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics count visiting the imprisoned among the corporal works of mercy, and many parishes run prison ministries; pilgrims to Toledo can visit the site associated with John's imprisonment.
